 ::JUDGMENT:

: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
SCCH-5 2

. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 02.10.2022 at about 4.15 p.m. petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-AZ- 5858 along with his friend as a pillion rider near Etlamavaripalle Village Bust Stop, on Madanapalle- Tirupathi Main Road, Annamayya District,
Andhra Pradesh, at that time, a Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-CZ- 0438 came from opposite direction at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle, due to the said impact, both petitioner and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Kalikiri, after first aid shifted to Sri Venkateshwara Institute of Medical Sciences, Tirupathi, further he took treatment as inpatient at Modern SCCH-5 Hospital, Madanapalle and he has spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medicine,
conveyance etc.,
3.

entities.text: Venkateshwara Institute of Medical Sciences, Tirupathi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 37 years, hale and healthy, working as agriculturist and driver, thereby earning Rs.25,000/-p.m.
Due to the accident, he is completely bedridden and lost his earnings.
With regard to accident in crime No.106/2022 is registered against the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-CA-0438 before the Voyalpad P.S. for the offences punishable under Sec.337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has not appeared before court hence placed exparte.
SCCH-5
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further respondent No.2 submitted that, Car bearing Reg. No. AP-39-CZ-0438 was not involved in the alleged accident and further submitted that, petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary and proper parties and rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-AZ-5858 without wearing helmet and without a valid and effective driving licence ride the said vehicle as on the date of accident.

Further submitted that, there is no jurisdiction to this tribunal to entertain this petition as the cause of action arose in Anamayya District, Andhra Pradesh and criminal case is registered at Voyalpad Police Station, Andhra Pradesh, the petitioner and 1st respondent resides at Andhra Pradesh and the policy issuing office also situated at Andhra Pradesh and the vehicles SCCH-5 Ramana .N vs Ammadasani Venkata Lakshmi on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95088083/
2 involved in the accident is registered at Andhra Pradesh, hence the petition against respondent No.2 is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.2 submitted that, it has issued policy of insurance in respect of Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-CZ-0438 in respect of respondent No.1 valid from 18.10.2019 to 17.10.2022 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to seek protection under Sec.147 and Sec.149 of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, on 02.10.2022 at about 4.15 p.m. when petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-AZ-5858 with SCCH-5 pillion rider G.Vishwanath Slowly on left side of Madanapalli - Thirupathi Road, near Etlamvaripalle Village

, at that time, one Car bearing Reg. No.AP- 39-CZ-0438 came from opposite side in high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle, as a result of which petitioner and pillion rider fell down and they have sustained severe injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?
If so from which respondent?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2 and marked 10 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.

On the other hand, Legal Officer of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
SCCH-5 7.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-

In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- Ramana .N vs Ammadasani Venkata Lakshmi on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95088083/
3 examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2,
copy of AIR as Ex.P.3, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.5.
SCCH-5 9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 02.10.2022 as alleged in the petition.
10. Per contra, Legal Officer of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy as Ex.R.2.
During the cross examination of R.W-1 he stated that rider of two wheeler attempted to overtake the car then alleged accident occurred.
R.W-1 stated that they have not conducted any investigation.
Except self serving statement no evidence to prove that accident occurred due to the fault of petitioner.

In the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained SCCH-5 the injuries due to the accident occurred on 02.10.2022 at about 4.15 p.m. when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.AP-03-AZ-5858 near Etlamvaripalle Village Bus Stop, on Madanapalle - Tirupathi Main Road, Annamayya District,
Andhra Pradesh.
11. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.AP-39-CZ-0438.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained cervical spine - C2 adontoid fracture, fracture medial malleolus right ankle, for which he took treatment of C2 adontoid screw fixation (ORIF SCCH-5 with anterior approach) and fracture medical malleolus right ankle was fixed with malleolar screw.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.4,
discharge summary marked as Ex.P.6 issued by Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences,
wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 03.10.2022 to 01.11.2022 and he also took treatment from 11.01.2023 to 23.01.2023 at Modern Hospital, Andhra Pradesh.
13.
Further Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD book marked as Ex.P.9 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.10 and he has assessed total disability of spine and right lower limb at 45% and that of his whole body disability at 23%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and on the basis of SCCH-5 wound certificate and discharge summaries, he has assessed the disability.
Further deposed that there are 2 fractures, one at C2 vertibral and another one is at right ankle and he has gone through MRI and CT Scan reports before surgery and post surgery.
Further deposed that, C-2 surgically operated by inserting screws and inserting screws itself is operating procedure for uniting fracture and now the fracture of C-2 is united properly.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 PW-2 deposed that, the spinal chord of the petitioner is normal and there is no neurological problem due to C-2 fracture and petitioner underwent physiotherapy and physiotherapy is an exercise for reduction of restriction of movements.

Further deposed that, fracture to ankle is not open fracture and ankle fracture is united within 12 weeks, it unites within a duration of 4 to 6 months and no document to show when the fracture is united.

Under SCCH-5 such circumstances,
considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 8% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 23% of total disability of spine and right lower limb, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 37 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.8, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 07.06.1986 and the alleged accident is occurred on 02.10.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.8 his age is considered about 37 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable as per decision reported SCCH-5 in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. As per his case, he was working as agriculturist,driver, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,500/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.6, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 03.10.2022 to 01.11.2022 and from 11.01.2023 to 23.01.2023 i.e., for 40 days.
As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined petitioner on 24.01.2025 i.e., nearly after 2 years 3 months and on examination date as per version of PW-2.
By considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least 4 months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.15,500/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for Rs.62,000/- towards loss on income during laid up period.

SCCH-5 17. Further on perusal of Ex.P.4 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that,
petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 02.10.2022. So as per Ex.P.4 Ramana .N vs Ammadasani Venkata Lakshmi on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95088083/
5 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained C2 odontoid fracture, which is grievous in nature.

Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.AP-39-CZ-0438 for the offences punishable under Sec.337, 338 of IPC.

The said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
18.
Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 2,23,200-00 SCCH-5 2.
Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 5. Loss of income during laid up 62,000-00 period Total 3,40,200-00 19.

Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,40,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

20. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.MOPL119050 valid from 18.10.2019 to 17.10.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 02.10.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent SCCH-5 No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
Hence this tribunal answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.3,40,200/-
(Rupees Three Lakhs Forty Thousand Two Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
